Many schemes are available by the state government for the farmers.Soil, seeds, irrigation, machinery, technology, credit, insurance, crop protection and marketing are important factors related to agriculture.If you need help with this, know about the various schemes offered by the state government.

Due to the financial need of the farmer and lack of adequate storage facilities at the local level, a large amount of agricultural produce is sold in the market during the harvesting season.Naturally, the market prices of farm produce come down.If the said agricultural produce is stored and brought for sale in the market after some time, the said agricultural produce can fetch higher market price.Therefore, the Agricultural Marketing Board has been implementing a farm collateral loan scheme since the year 1990-91 with a view to ensure that the farmers get a fair price for their produce.Under this scheme, agricultural produce such as tur, moong, urad, soybean, sunflower, gram, rice paddy, sorghum, sorghum, millet, maize, wheat, tiger nut, cashew seed, currant, betel nut and turmeric have been included and under this scheme, farmers can get up to 75 percent of the total price of the agricultural produce deposited in the warehouse of the market committee.The mortgage loan is given at 6 percent interest rate for a period of 180 days.Under this scheme, mortgage loan is also provided to the farmers on the warehouse receipt of the State or Central Wakhar Corporation.The scheme is implemented through market committees and 3 percent interest concession is given to the market committees who repay the mortgage loan within six months.

scheme_name: Subsidy Scheme for Export of Agricultural Produce by Sea
description: As the distance of some countries is more from India, fruits and vegetables are exported by air.Air fares are high for transportation.Therefore, the goods have to be sold at a higher price in the foreign market.Export by sea option is available on this.However, if the goods are to be exported by sea, it takes more time.As the fruits and vegetables are perishable, the exporter is not willing to export by sea.Due to this, it is necessary to encourage the export of some agricultural products by sea.In order to get the maximum incentive for the export of agricultural goods from Maharashtra, a scheme was proposed through the Maharashtra State Agricultural Marketing Board to provide subsidy for international transport of agricultural goods by sea.

scheme_name: Fruits and Grains Festival Subsidy Scheme
description: The scheme is implemented to organize festivals for direct producer-to-consumer sale of seasonal fruits and grains like mangoes, oranges, mangoes, grapes.

Maharashtra is a leader in the production of fruits and vegetables. Specially, tomatoes, pomegranates, grapes, bananas, mangoes and vegetables are produced in the state on a large scale.Since fruits and vegetables are perishable, about 20 to 30 percent of agricultural produce is lost due to improper handling and delays during transportation. Looking at the production of fruits and vegetables in Maharashtra, as domestic trade is also important along with export, it is necessary to promote direct trade of the agricultural produce produced in the state by getting a market outside the state.Farmer Cooperative Societies producing agricultural products as well as Farmers producing companies FPC.Many times, there are restrictions on sending perishable agricultural goods to foreign countries due to not being able to afford the transport costs. In order to promote the inter-state trade of agricultural goods in the state through agricultural production companies and cooperative societies of agricultural products, the issue of subsidizing the transport costs was under the consideration of the Marketing Board.
